title: progressive-routing-and-fallbacks-for-variant-incompatibility-across-regions-and-capacity-tiers
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a deterministic routing and fallback subsystem to support progressive rollouts (canaries, A/B tests, shadow traffic) while handling model-variant compatibility mismatches, region failovers, and tiered capacity degradation. The system must allow safe exposure of new model variants with automated rollback triggers, preserve strict latency SLOs for P99 and signal degradations early via synthetic and production probes.

Scope and requirements:
- Routing modes: canary (percent-based), A/B (sticky cookie/session-based), shadow (replicated traffic for offline evaluation).
- Compatibility checks: runtime-level feature matrix and fast pre-flight compatibility scoring for model artifacts (KV cache layout, tokenizers, function-call schemas).
- Tiered capacity awareness: route requests by customer tier (hosted/dedicated/private) and degrade gracefully (e.g., fall back to quantized variant, lower context window, or secondary region).
- Region failover policy: proximity-aware failover with warm-standby capacity and regional compatibility validation before traffic shift.
- Auto-rollback: multi-signal trigger based on error rate/latency regressions, semantic regression score from evaluation set, and customer complaint black-box signals.
- Observability: per-route metrics (errors, latencies, token-cost), canary-specific dashboards, and automated post-mortem links for rollbacks.

Non-goals:
- Full model retraining workflows.
- Replacing infra-level autoscaling (this system will call existing autoscaler APIs).
acceptance_criteria:
1) New routing subsystem accepts a rollout plan that includes percent, sticky, or shadow modes and applies it traffic-wide.
2) Compatibility pre-flight returns a score for each variant and rejects incompatible combinations with human-review reason.
3) On regional capacity loss, traffic shifts to configured fallback regions respecting tier preferences and quantified latency impact (must be surfaced).
4) Auto-rollback triggers on: sustained P99 latency > 2x baseline for 3m, error rate spike > 1% absolute for 5m, or semantic-quality drop > 5% on canary eval set.
5) Rollback actions record rationale, related PRs, and generate an incident-summary stub in the console.
design_notes:
Compatibility scoring algorithm: combine static artifact checks (tokenizer version, model schema) with lightweight runtime probes (warm KV cache probe, short-run inference smoke tests) into 0-100 score. Thresholds: <50 auto-block; 50-75 warn and require approver; >75 auto-allow.

Fallback hierarchy (priority order): 1) Same-region compatible variant (quantized or smaller) 2) Nearby-region compatible variant 3) Global compatible fallback model (higher latency, lower cost model) 4) Degrade response (trim context / reduce completion length)

Rollback orchestration: atomic flag flip in routing graph, with gradual deceleration of canary traffic (80% -> 50% -> 0% over 90s) while routing engine verifies reduction in error/latency and emits audit logs.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive auto-rollback reduces blast radius but can cause oscillation for noisy metrics; we use multi-signal hysteresis and require at least 2 signals or manual confirmation for high-impact customers. Shadow traffic must be throttled to avoid double billing; implemented as best-effort asynchronous replication to offline evaluators.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): routing graph model + canary percent engine + compatibility pre-flight basic checks; unit tests and API.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): A/B sticky routing, shadow mode with async mirror pipeline, dashboard basics.
Phase 3 (3 weeks): tiered capacity rules, region failover automation hooks, synthetic probes.
Phase 4 (2 weeks): auto-rollback policy engine, audit trails, safety gates, and e2e load tests.
Phase 5 (1 week): gradual rollout to staging customers and documentation.
risks:
- False positives on compatibility checks may block safe rollouts causing churn. Mitigation: allow manual override with audit.
- Oscillation due to noisy metrics; mitigation: hysteresis windows and require correlated signals.
- Shadow traffic cost and privacy: ensure data filtering and opt-in for customers.
- Cross-region legal/privacy constraints: integrate region constraints into routing policy.
metrics_and_slos:
Primary metrics: canary error rate, canary P95/P99 latency, semantic-regression-on-eval, rollback frequency.
SLOs: P99 under rollout must remain within 1.8x of baseline for non-high-tier customers and within 1.2x for enterprise tiers.
Alerting: pager on >2x baseline P99 for 10m or rollback frequency > 3 in 24h for same model.
